answer: Neighborhood-hash admission. Each agent's address derives from hashes of its declared neighbors; a new node is admitted only if its neighbor set overlaps the existing graph enough to form closed triangles. Cheap duplicate clusters stay isolated because they share no external edges, so their votes never ripple into the main component. Honest agents sit in a dense haven of cross-links, while a sybil swarm must spend real effort recruiting genuine bridge edges against a continuous gale of random neighbor challenges, paying per-identity discovery and link-maintenance costs.
